# Vaisakh Rajeev

I am a physicist working in **observational cosmology and
large-scale structure**, with research spanning astronomical surveys,
cosmological simulations, galaxy–halo modelling, and time-domain
astronomy.

I recently completed my Ph.D. in Physics at **Southern Methodist
University**, where I worked with Dr. Robert Kehoe on measurements of
cosmic expansion using quasars, galaxies, and local supernovae.

</div>


## Research experience

### Southern Methodist University

**Ph.D. in Physics**  
2020–2026

Advisor: Dr. Robert Kehoe

Dissertation:

*Measuring Cosmic Expansion from Early to Late Times using Quasars,
Galaxies, and Local Supernovae*

My doctoral research included DESI mock-catalog production and
clustering validation, galaxy–halo connection modelling, survey
systematics, redshift-failure modelling, and Type Ib/c supernova
cosmology.


### Indian Institute of Technology Hyderabad

**M.Sc. Physics**  
2017–2019

M.Sc. thesis:

*Tests of Violation of Inverse Square Law on Radio Pulsar Fluxes*

Advisor: Dr. Shantanu Desai.


### University of Delhi

**B.Sc. (Honors) Physics**  
2014–2017


## DESI

I have been involved with the **Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument
(DESI)** as a collaborator and support observer.

My DESI work includes mock-catalog production, clustering analyses,
observational-systematics studies, and survey operations.

I have contributed more than **1500 hours of DESI service**, including
observing operations, software maintenance, analysis infrastructure,
and systematic-effects studies.

I have also participated in more than **50 remote and in-person
observing shifts**.

## Teaching & mentoring

I have taught and supported undergraduate physics courses at
Southern Methodist University, including mechanics, electromagnetism,
and introductory physics laboratories.

I have also mentored undergraduate and graduate students working on
topics including DESI science, ROTSE photometry, near-infrared
astronomy, and observational astronomy.


## Scientific computing

My research relies heavily on scientific computing and large-scale
data analysis.

**Languages & tools**

Python · NumPy · SciPy · pandas · Astropy · Matplotlib · Jupyter ·
Bash · LaTeX

**Computing & data**

HPC · SLURM · Git/GitHub · FITS · HDF5 · Parquet · large-scale
catalog processing · simulation workflows

**Methods**

Galaxy–halo modelling · HOD · subhalo modelling · clustering
statistics · covariance estimation · forward modelling · systematic
uncertainty analysis
